claims.text: The material is a magnetic high-entropy alloy with a single-phase solid-solution structure.
Increasing the number of alloy constituents increases configurational entropy.
Increased configurational entropy stabilizes disordered solid-solution phases relative to ordered intermetallic phases.
Increasing the number of constituents reduces the formation of intermetallic compounds.
Stabilizing solid solutions and suppressing intermetallic compounds increases the coercive field.
The coercive field increases as the number of constituents increases.
The proposed effect holds when composition and processing conditions are kept constant.
The exact relationship between constituent count and coercive field is not well established.
Lattice strain and grain size may affect coercive field, but their effects are not considered.

contradictions.description: Increasing the number of distinct constituents necessarily changes the elemental composition or redistributes elemental fractions, so it cannot literally be done while keeping alloy composition constant as stated.
The same two evidence records are simultaneously designated as supporting and conflicting evidence without an explanation of which claims they support or contradict.
